comments: Child denies the implicit proposition in Father's prompt 'la cuchara y el tenedor ?' and asserts ownership; Father's follow-up 'son tuyos ?' confirms the factual nature of the exchange.
Child reports inability to attach the steering wheel; a claim about ability is Denial per rule 5.
Child confirms the father's question 'no funciona ?' regarding the toy's functionality; this is a factual claim.
Child interrupts father's storytelling to take over the turn ('no, yo'), blocking the father's action.
The token 'na' is a false start/fragment of the word 'nave' (spaceship), not a negation.
Child makes a factual claim that the spaceship does not work to explain a character's behavior.
Child contradicts the adult's claim that Bobi is in the pool (line 57161).
Child disagrees with the father's confirmation ('claro') in line 58392.
Child vetoes a puzzle piece placement in response to father's question about where it goes.
The token 'sin' is part of a transcription note [= articula sin voz] describing the child's voice, not a spoken negation.
Child resists mother's directive to use the fork (line 96839).
Child refuses mother's request to eat more slowly (line 96912); mother's follow-up 'tienes prisa?' (line 96916) confirms it was heard as a refusal.
The token appears to be a fragment of an overlap with the parent's subsequent turn ('no es que son de juguete') or a self-repair, not a functional negation act.
Child denies the father's assertion that it is June; father's response 'sí' confirms a factual dispute.
Child says 'no' as the dog approaches, attempting to stop the dog's action.
Child denies the caregiver's claim that the animal is a tiger (line 113690), followed by a question about its identity.
Child states they do not know the animal; a factual claim about their state of knowledge.
Child confirms dislike of the story in response to the caregiver's question 'éste no te gusta?'; this is a claim about preference.
The child denies the caregiver's claim that the object is a deer (line 113901) and corrects it to an elephant.
Child denies the caregiver's identification of the animal as a beaver (line 113998).
Child echoes the caregiver's previous turn ('no, eso es un elefante'), repeating the negation and the noun as a contentless echo.
Child rejects the caregiver's proposal to look at the books ('vamos a_ver estos cuentos') by asserting they are already doing so.
Child responds to the question 'y esto qué es ?' by stating they do not know; this is a factual claim about their knowledge.
The child denies the adult's claim that the object is 'tu pelo' (your hair) and corrects it by pointing to something else ('ésta').
Child contradicts Father's claim that vultures were big, immediately re-asserting they were 'pequeños'.
Child refuses the adult's request to lend the car ('préstamelo').
The child is reporting that the uncle (quillis) is not present, which is a claim of absence.
Child continues to describe the game, repeating the negative assertion from line 185302 ('y esto no') about the placement/action of an object.
Child states that an object does not fit ('no cabe'), which is a claim about the world.
Child refuses the action of going to the car, as seen in 'a coche no' and mother's uptake 'no quieres al coche?'
Child refuses the mother's proposal to go to the car ('al coche ?'), as evidenced by the preceding 'a coche no'.
The child makes a factual assertion that the toy mosquito is no longer falling; the father's echo 'ya no cae?' confirms it as a truth claim.
Child refuses the mother's directive to lie down and sleep (lines 309840, 309843).
Child asserts the absence of people, following the mother's earlier question 'no hay nadie' and her later comment 'no se vea nada'.
Child uses 'nadie' to express absence of objects in the sky, as interpreted by MOT in line 447934 ('no se vea nada').
Child says 'not here', likely vetoing a proposed location or action; mother's subsequent 'what do you want?' suggests a refusal was heard.
Child denies mother's claim that the chicken is raw/inedible after she asks 'ves?' (do you see?).
Child refuses the food the mother is encouraging them to eat (mira como se lo come mamá).
Child refuses the mother's directive to put the stroller inside ('mete en casa el carrito').
